subtitle: Cross-reading for 3 September 2026, the day's closing reading: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) price from the confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 23:45 BRT (04/Sep, 02:45 UTC), presidential book at USD 142.61M, against the Datafolha poll of 03/Sep (BR-03669/2026, field 01 to 03/Sep, n=2,002, margin of 2pp), the third national poll in 48 hours. ⭐ ALL THREE DISAGREE ON THE SIGN OF THE [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) between the top two: Genial/Quaest of 02/Sep put the leader ahead by 42% to 41%, PoderData of 03/Sep put the runner-up ahead by 45% to 44%, and Datafolha of 03/Sep puts the leader ahead by 46% to 44%. ⭐ AND DATAFOLHA IS THE FOURTH TOP-TIER HOUSE TO MEASURE AUGUSTO CURY'S JUMP AND THE ONLY ONE THAT LEAVES HIM BELOW DOUBLE DIGITS. In the price, the only name in the presidential book to move since 17:28 was the runner-up.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 54.50% (vol USD 9.67M accumulated), confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 23:45 BRT (04/Sep, 02:45 UTC), unchanged since today's 15:22 reading, meaning his price has not moved for more than eight hours. POLL: the Datafolha poll of 03/Sep (BR-03669/2026, field 01 to 03/Sep, n=2,002, margin of 2pp) gives him 39% in the scenario with Pablo Marçal and 38% in the one without. In the second round he beats the runner-up by 46% to 44%, Ronaldo Caiado by 46% to 41% and Romeu Zema by 48% to 39%.
fortes: He wins the three second-round pairings with figures published by Datafolha, and the house tested a fourth, against Renan Santos, which he also wins.
In the first-round scenario with Marçal he repeats the 39% of the house's own round of 21/Aug, without giving ground.
In the first-round runner-up contract he rose 1.80pp and stands at 10.50% (vol USD 439 thousand), his largest gain in any contract in this reading.
His price did not give ground in either of today's readings, even with his opponent rising in both.

He declared the [INSS](/en/glossary#inss) queue cleared at a ceremony at the Planalto Palace, and requests running more than 45 days late fell 86% since January, from 1.88 million to 261 thousand in August, according to Metrópoles and Poder360.
fracos: ⚠️ AT DATAFOLHA THE SECOND-ROUND GAP HALVED WITHIN THE HOUSE: 46% to 44% now, against 47% to 43% on 21/Aug, that is, from 4 to 2 points, and it now fits inside the declared margin of 2pp.
In the scenario without Marçal he gave up from 39% to 38% within Datafolha itself, while his opponent held at 33%.
Government disapproval at Datafolha is 51%, against 45% approval, and disapproval is 3 points higher than what Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) measured on 02/Sep.
His gap to the runner-up in the price fell to 11.65pp, against 16.55pp on 01/Sep, and it has narrowed across four consecutive readings since.
PoderData the same day puts him behind in the second round, 44% to 45%, which makes the window's three houses two in his favour and one against, all inside the margin.
candidates.analise: His day ends with three measurements and none of them moves him in the price. Datafolha confirms the lead in all four second-round pairings it tested, but halves the gap in the main pairing within the house itself, from 4 to 2 points between 21/Aug and now. PoderData the same day places him behind in that pairing, and Genial/Quaest the day before placed him ahead by 1 point. Three houses, three results, and all inside the declared margin, which means none of them asserts a lead. In the price he is the opposite of that: 54.50% at 15:22, at 17:28 and now, more than eight hours without moving, while the gap to the runner-up narrows through movement on the other side. What changes on his side outside the ballot is the [INSS](/en/glossary#inss), with the ceremony held and the criterion stated by the minister.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 42.85% (vol USD 9.64M accumulated), confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 23:45 BRT (04/Sep, 02:45 UTC), up 0.35pp on the 17:28 reading, and it was the ONLY name in the presidential book to move over the interval. The gap to the leader fell to 11.65pp. POLL: the Datafolha poll of 03/Sep (BR-03669/2026, field 01 to 03/Sep, n=2,002, margin of 2pp) gives him 32% in the scenario with Marçal and 33% in the one without, and 44% in a second round in which the leader has 46%.
fortes: ⭐ HE WAS THE ONLY NAME OUT OF THE PRESIDENTIAL BOOK'S NINETEEN TO MOVE between the 17:28 reading and the closing one, and the move was upward.
The gap to the leader fell to 11.65pp and has narrowed across four consecutive readings since 01/Sep, when it was 16.55pp.
At Datafolha he closes to 2 points in the second round, 44% against 46%, after 43% against 47% in the same house's round of 21/Aug.
PoderData the same day puts him numerically ahead in that pairing, 45% to 44%, for the first time in that house's three rounds since 13/Aug.
fracos: In the Datafolha first round he repeats the same 32% and 33% of 21/Aug, meaning he did not advance within the house in two weeks.
⚠️ In the first-round runner-up contract he gave up 2.00pp and stands at 83.50%, his largest fall in any contract in this reading.
The 1-point lead PoderData gives him in the second round sits inside the declared margin, and the window's other two houses give the pairing to the leader.
His rejection rate is still the highest among the thirteen names tested by Genial/Quaest on 02/Sep, at 55%.
candidates.analise: He was the only move in the presidential book in the day's closing hours, up 0.35pp, and it is the fourth consecutive close in which the gap to the leader narrows. In declared voting intention the picture is more ambiguous than the price suggests: Datafolha keeps him at the same 32% and 33% of two weeks ago in the first round, and at the same time cuts the second-round gap from 4 to 2 points within the house itself. PoderData the same day puts him ahead in that pairing and Genial/Quaest the day before put him behind. Three houses, three signals, none outside the margin. And in the first-round runner-up contract, where he has dominated for weeks, is where he gave up the most in this reading.

candidates.name: Augusto Cury
candidates.header: PRICE: 1.25% (vol USD 3.69M accumulated) in the WINNER contract, confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 23:45 BRT (04/Sep, 02:45 UTC), down 0.10pp. In the first-round THIRD-PLACE contract, which is a different market, he rose 3.60pp and stands at 59.50%, in a book of 114 thousand dollars accumulated. POLL: ⭐ the Datafolha poll of 03/Sep (BR-03669/2026, field 01 to 03/Sep, n=2,002, margin of 2pp) IS THE FOURTH TOP-TIER HOUSE TO MEASURE THE JUMP AND THE ONLY ONE THAT LEAVES HIM BELOW DOUBLE DIGITS, at 7% in the scenario with Marçal and 8% in the one without, against 2% in the house's own round of 21/Aug.
fortes: ⭐ FIVE HOUSES MEASURED THE JUMP SINCE 31/Aug, and all in the same direction: BTG/Nexus 11% on 31/Aug, Real Time Big Data 11% on 01/Sep, Genial/Quaest 10% on 02/Sep, PoderData 10% on 03/Sep and Datafolha 7% and 8% across its two scenarios the same day.
Within Datafolha itself he went from 2% on 21/Aug to 7% and 8% now, the largest advance of any name at that house between the two rounds.
In the first-round third-place contract he rose 3.60pp and stands at 59.50%, a third straight day of gains, and opened 37.50pp over that market's second name.
His rejection rate is 25% at Genial/Quaest on 02/Sep, the lowest among the seven most prominent names tested.
fracos: ⚠️ THE LEVEL IS NOT THE SAME ACROSS HOUSES, and the difference is large: four houses put him at 10% or 11% and Datafolha puts him at 7% and 8%. Anyone reading a single house comes away with a different picture from anyone reading another.
In the winner contract he gave up 0.10pp and stands at 1.25%, meaning the price that asks who wins the election did not follow any of this.
In the first-round runner-up contract he gave up 0.70pp and stands at 1.75%.
Datafolha did not test a second round with him, so the only second-round reading in the base is still the Genial/Quaest one of 02/Sep, in which he loses by 40% to 34%.
Folha de S.Paulo itself framed his day under the argument that the campaign wiped out the Dark Horse effect, which is a reading about a ceiling rather than an advance.
candidates.analise: Datafolha changes his picture without changing the direction. Five houses measured the jump since 31/Aug and all five point the same way, but four put him in double digits and this one puts him at 7% and 8%. Within Datafolha itself the advance is the largest of any name between 21/Aug and now, from 2% to 8%, so there is no contradiction of direction: there is disagreement about level, and it is three to four points. The comparison that counts is still each house against itself, because adding up yardsticks from different institutes is what produces false precision. In the price, the winner contract gave up 0.10pp and the first-round third-place contract rose 3.60pp for a third straight day. The market keeps buying third place and not the election.

In declared voting intention Datafolha keeps him at 4% in the scenario with Marçal and cuts him to 3% in the one without, and against the same house's 21/Aug round he gives ground in the second scenario. In the price, the 4.50pp fall in the third-place contract is the panel's largest in this reading, and it comes on the same day Augusto Cury rose 3.60pp in the same market: the gap between the two in that contract went from 29.40pp to 37.50pp in a few hours. Marina Silva argued that Moraes should step aside, according to Metrópoles.

cruzamento: The close of 3 September brings together three measurements that do not reconcile, and that is what this page records. ⭐ THE FIRST IS THE SIGN OF THE SECOND ROUND. Three national houses published within 48 hours and disagree on who wins the pairing between the top two: Genial/Quaest of 02/Sep put the leader ahead by 42% to 41%, PoderData of 03/Sep put the runner-up ahead by 45% to 44%, and Datafolha of 03/Sep puts the leader ahead by 46% to 44%. All three margins are 1 or 2 points and all three houses declare a margin of error of 2pp, so none of them asserts a lead outside the margin. The panel records all three and does not choose. ⭐ THE SECOND IS AUGUSTO CURY'S LEVEL, and it is new. Five houses measured his jump since 31/Aug: BTG/Nexus 11% on 31/Aug, Real Time Big Data 11% on 01/Sep, Genial/Quaest 10% on 02/Sep, PoderData 10% on 03/Sep and Datafolha 7% and 8% across its two scenarios the same day. Four put him in double digits and Datafolha puts him at 7% and 8%. The jump appears in all of them, because within Datafolha itself he went from 2% on 21/Aug; what changes between houses is the size of the level, not the direction. ⚠️ AND THE FIRMEST READING HERE IS THE ONE WITHIN EACH HOUSE, not the average across them, because adding up yardsticks from different institutes is what produces false precision. THE THIRD IS THE PRICE, and it barely moved. Between the 17:28 reading and the closing one, a single name out of the presidential book's nineteen moved: the runner-up, up 0.35pp to 42.85%. The leader is still at 54.50% and has not moved for more than eight hours. The gap between the two fell to 11.65pp, against 12.00pp at 17:28, 14.85pp on 02/Sep and 16.55pp on 01/Sep. In the side markets the move was larger than in the main one: in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) runner-up contract the runner-up gave up 2.00pp, to 83.50%, and the leader rose 1.80pp, to 10.50%; and in the third-place contract Augusto Cury rose 3.60pp, to 59.50%, while Renan Santos gave up 4.50pp, to 22.00%, the panel's largest fall in this reading. ⚠️ THIS ROUND PUBLISHES NO NEW PRICE FOR THE [SUPREME COURT](/en/glossary#stf) IMPEACHMENT CONTRACT. Its last confirmed reading is the 03/Sep one at 17:28, at 7.40%, and that is the one the page keeps. 📌 The contrast that closes the day: the crisis at the Supreme Court produced this Thursday the harshest act in the series, with one justice asking for another to be investigated, and the price of the contract that measures a justice leaving is the only one on the panel with no new reading to publish.
